summary: CCC-built 79-ft-6-in tower on Dairy Hill, closed 1986; sources disagree on removal (1991 list vs 1992 sale and move); no source describes the summit today.

facts.design: 79-foot-6-inch International Derrick steel tower provided to New York State by the US Forest Service, with an enclosed metal cab
facts.status_note: Removed after vandalism. The Searchable list gives 1991; the Eastern lookouts site says it was sold and moved in 1992.

events.note: CCC built the tower; provided to the state by the US Forest Service
Herkimer County site purchase per a January 1934 newspaper report; the 1942 survey says the land was state-owned
First staffed in 1935, reporting 6 fires and 568 visitors
Fire lookout operations ceased; tower and cabin later removed after extreme vandalism
Searchable list gives 1991 as the removal year
Eastern lookouts site says the 82-foot tower was sold and moved to a new location

corrections.why: The Searchable list and Wikipedia both give 79 ft 6 in (24.23 m). The 25.0 m figure matches the 82-foot number that appears only on the Eastern lookouts site.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Removal and fate conflict: the Searchable list and Wikipedia say the tower and cabin were removed after vandalism (1991 on the list); the Eastern site says it was sold and moved in 1992. The story reports both without choosing.
Two sources say 79 ft 6 in, the Eastern site says 82 ft, and the 1942 survey says about 80 ft. The record uses 79 ft 6 in.

Descriptions differ: five miles east of Newport (Searchable list), southeast of Norway (Wikipedia), and about eight miles northwest of Salisbury (1942 survey). The sites may use different reference points.
The January 1934 newspaper report says Herkimer County bought the site; the 1942 survey says the land belonged to New York State.

sources.title: Searchable list of NY Fire Towers

notes_for_editor: Height, location, land ownership and removal date all conflict across the sources; the story reports the conflicts rather than choosing a version. The 1992 sale appears only on the Eastern lookouts site; a web search did not confirm it. Wikipedia and the directory give coordinates about 1.5 km apart (Wikipedia 43.1912, -74.8971; directory 43.20372, -74.90367); check before any visit. Nothing read describes the summit today.
